metadata.note: The Atlanta, Birmingham & Atlantic (1906-1926) and its successor the Atlanta, Birmingham & Coast (1926-1946), with their predecessors and the ACL/SCL years after the 1946 merger: Atlanta - Manchester - Cordele - Fitzgerald - Waycross (the Dixie route), Manchester - LaGrange - Talladega - Birmingham, Nicholls - Brunswick and Fitzgerald - Tifton - Thomasville, plus the affiliated Alabama Northern (Pyriton - Ashland) as a single-year anchor. Every feature is drawn only for the report's drawable span, split by operator (Rule 4); features for successive operators of one line share identical geometry.
metadata.ownership_split: Waycross Air Line -> Atlantic & Birmingham Railroad (rename 27 Nov 1901) -> Atlantic & Birmingham Railway (consolidation 3 Dec 1903, with the Tifton & Northeastern and Tifton, Thomasville & Gulf; bought the Brunswick & Birmingham 6 Sept 1904): the WAL/A&B RR/A&B Ry are treated as ONE company and colour (a rename and a consolidation led by the same road), while the T&NE, TT&G and B&B are split at 1903/1904. -> AB&A, merger effective 1 May 1906 (split 1906). NOT splits: the 1915 (railga) / 1914 (Wikipedia) Railroad -> Railway reorganization and the 1909-1926 receiverships. -> AB&C 1926 (split 1926, the report's recommendation: foreclosure reorganization into a new company under ACL control; a reviewer could treat AB&A/AB&C as one). The ACL's 1926/27 stock control is NOT a split - the AB&C ran its own trains. -> ACL 1946 (merger; 1945 per Wikipedia's ACL article - conflict recorded, only the colour split moves). -> SCL 1 July 1967 (Atlanta - Waycross only; Birmingham trains ended 1954).
metadata.omitted: Bushnell - Ocilla (Brunswick & Birmingham, 19 mi): drawable NONE - no confirmable passenger year, and its existence after Nov 1905 is disputed (ICC abandoned Nov 1905 vs railga). Ocilla - Irwinville: AB&A-owned but operated by the Ocilla & Valdosta / Fitzgerald, Ocilla & Broxton / Ocilla Southern - not AB&A trains. Irwinville - Alapaha River, Offerman & Western before July 1902, Waycross Air Line logging years 1890-1893, Eastern Ry of Alabama, Alabama Terminal Mulga branch and Bessemer - Aglum Yard: freight/logging only (Rule 1). The AB&A's Sept 1908 - July 1910 route into Birmingham (probably L&N trackage from Pelham) is unverified and not drawn. The Georgia Terminal Co. track into Atlanta Terminal Station is a labelled straight leg.
not_yet_sourced: END YEARS 1969 (Atlanta - Waycross) and 1954 (Manchester - Birmingham) rest on secondary sources only (chicagorailfan.com station pages, plus Wikipedia's Dixie Flyer article for 1969). Primary confirmation stops at the Official Guide of Feb 1952 (Dec 13 1951 schedules). A 1957-1968 ACL/SCL public timetable or an ICC discontinuance docket would settle both.

The 1957-1969 Dixie Flyer routing over this line is INFERRED: Wikipedia's Dixie Flyer text describes a CofG Atlanta-Macon-Albany + ACL Albany-Tifton-Waycross routing, while its route map and chicagorailfan's 1942 column put the Dixie Flyer on the ACL (ex-AB&C) Atlanta - Waycross line.

[OPEN] ends: Nicholls - Brunswick drawn to 1918, Fitzgerald - Tifton - Thomasville to 1917 - last CONFIRMED years from the April 1918 Official Guide; both were 'Freight Service only' by Dec 1951 and the real passenger ends are unknown (a 1930s-40s Official Guide AB&C page, or Goolsby's 'Atlanta, Birmingham & Coast', ACL & SAL Historical Society 2000, would move them).
[OPEN] starts: Douglas - Waycross 1900 (bracket 1893-1900; WAL timetables of 1895/1899 unseen), Montezuma - Fitzgerald 1904 (bracket 1902/1903-1904), Tifton - Thomasville 1901 (bracket 1899-1901).
The 1903/1904-1906 Atlantic & Birmingham years on the Brunswick and Thomasville lines have no passenger timetable of their own; drawn between confirmed years under the companies either side.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.
metadata.source_conflicts: Merger into the ACL 1946 (railga; Wikipedia AB&C) vs 1945 (Wikipedia ACL); ACL control 1926 vs 1927; AB&A Railroad -> Railway reorganization 1915 (railga) vs 1914 (Wikipedia); Nicholls - Douglas opened 1898 (ICC) vs 1900 (railga); Bushnell - Ocilla abandoned 1905 (ICC) vs still AB&A (railga/Fowler). None moves a drawn year except where stated.
metadata.freight_only: Rule 1: Nicholls - Brunswick and Fitzgerald - Thomasville stop at their last confirmed passenger years, not at the 1951 freight-only listing nor the 1960 abandonment.

segments.note: The Waycross Air Line (Waycross - Sessoms 1890 as a logging road, common carrier by 1893; Sessoms - Nicholls 1897; Nicholls - Douglas 1898 per the ICC, 1900 per railga.com - conflict recorded). Drawn from 1900, the first CONFIRMED passenger year: Fowler tags Upchurch (Sessoms - Waycross) '1900G' and Chatterton (Nicholls - Douglas) '[Bell 1900Glist]', both listed in the 1900 Official Guide. 1900 is an [OPEN] start - railga lists WAL timetables of 1895 and 1899 that were not seen; do not move it earlier without evidence. The Waycross Air Line was RENAMED the Atlantic & Birmingham Railroad on 27 Nov 1901 and consolidated with the Tifton & Northeastern and Tifton, Thomasville & Gulf as the Atlantic & Birmingham Railway on 3 Dec 1903; treated as one company throughout (a rename and a consolidation led by the same road, same trains), so one colour. Ends 1906: merged into the Atlanta, Birmingham & Atlantic effective 1 May 1906. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the train count, not a sourced headway.

segments.note: Atlanta, Birmingham & Coast Railroad, the 1926 foreclosure reorganization of the AB&A under Atlantic Coast Line stock control (control 1926 per railga and Wikipedia's AB&C article; 1927 per Wikipedia's ACL article). The ACL's stock purchase did NOT change who ran the trains: the AB&C ran its own passenger trains under its own name until the merger (Wikipedia AB&C), so this is AB&C, not ACL, colour. Atlanta terminal moved from Terminal Station to Union Station Nov 1933. Dixieland Atlanta - Waycross from Jan 1936; Dixie Flagler (Chicago - Miami, every third day) from Dec 1940; 1942: Nos. 1/2, 3/4 (Dixie Flyer) and 11/12 (Dixie Flagler) (chicagorailfan). Ends 1946: merged into the ACL as its Western Division - 1946 per railga and Wikipedia's AB&C article, 1945 per Wikipedia's ACL article (CONFLICT recorded; this moves only the colour split, not any drawn year). Splitting AB&A -> AB&C at 1926 follows the report's recommendation (new company, new control, new name); a reviewer could treat it as one company. headway_min is an ESTIMATE from the train count, not a sourced headway.
sources: Segment-level: per the research report, Wikipedia AB&C and Dixie Flagler articles (trains and dates); chicagorailfan 1942 column; merger date per railga/Wikipedia (conflict recorded). Secondary sources only for this era.
